I am registering your request in our ticketing system.
A customer has explained a support need. Tell them formally that you are recording the request in the team's ticketing system.
Ons agrees with singular het ticketsysteem. Registering a request is not the same as approving or solving it.
Could you give your ticket number?
A customer contacts support about a previous request. Ask formally for the ticket number so you can locate the existing record.
The reference identifies an existing support request. It is not a password or one-time security code.
What can I help you with today?
You have answered a customer's support call. Address the caller formally and ask what help they need today.
Waarmee combines waar and met to ask about the matter needing help. U is the person receiving help.
S=Ik|V=maak|O=een aparte melding voor dit probleem|PART=aan.
I am creating a separate report for this problem.
A customer raises another problem during an existing request. Tell them formally that this problem will receive its own report.
Aparte separates this problem from the earlier one. Maak ... aan is a separable verb.
Have you contacted our service desk before?
A customer reports an issue without saying whether support has already been involved. Ask formally whether they contacted the service desk before.
Hebt u is a valid formal inversion. Contact opnemen met is a fixed expression; the question concerns previous contact, not previous resolution.
I have just received your report.
A customer checks whether a recently submitted report arrived. Confirm formally that you have just received it.
Zojuist means just now. Receipt does not automatically establish that you have understood or resolved the report.
MOD=Mag|S=ik|I=vragen|G=op welk nummer u bereikbaar bent?
May I ask on which number you can be reached?
You may need to call a customer back about their request. Ask formally which business phone number can be used to reach them.
Op welk nummer is an embedded contact question. It requests a contact number, not a verification code.
Your request will receive its own ticket number.
A customer wants to know how their new request will be tracked. Explain formally that it will get its own reference number.
The present describes the registration procedure and its expected next result. Eigen means its own, not a secret or private number.
S=Ik|V=zie|O=uw eerdere melding|NEG=nog niet|L=in het overzicht.
I do not yet see your earlier report in the overview.
A customer says a previous report exists, but it is not visible in your current list. Explain formally what you can currently see.
Nog niet describes the current view; it does not accuse the customer of failing to submit the report.
S=Ik|V=noteer|O=deze gegevens|TE=om uw vraag bij het juiste team te krijgen.
I am noting these details so your request can reach the right team.
A customer asks why you are recording basic request details. Explain formally that the details help route their request to the appropriate team.
Om gives a routing purpose. Recording details does not by itself resolve the issue.
Which application are you using when this happens?
A customer describes an unexpected event without naming the software. Ask formally which application they are using at that moment.
Wanneer identifies the occurrence being discussed. The question does not assume a specific application caused it.
What exactly do you see on your screen?
A customer reports unexpected screen behaviour. Ask formally for an exact description of what is visible.
Ziet agrees with formal u. The question asks for an observation, not a diagnosis.
MOD=Kunt|S=u|O=de stappen tot aan de foutmelding|I=beschrijven?
Could you describe the steps leading up to the error message?
A customer has reached an error message while using an application. Ask formally which actions preceded that point.
Tot aan identifies the sequence up to the message. It does not establish that the final action caused the fault.
When did the problem first begin?
A customer has a recurring problem but has not said when it started. Ask about its first occurrence.
Wanneer is a question word, not a past verb. Begon is the finite past form; voor het eerst asks about onset.
V=Werkt|S=u|T=nu|L=op kantoor of van thuis uit?
Are you working at the office or from home now?
You need the location context of a customer's current issue. Ask formally whether they are at the office or working from home now.
The present context is now, not a general weekly schedule. Van thuis uit is common standard Belgian wording.
Which device do you use for this task?
A customer has trouble completing a task that can be done on several devices. Ask formally which device they use for it.
Welk modifies singular het toestel. The question identifies the device, not its ownership or authorisation.
Could you indicate whether other users experience the same thing?
A customer reports an issue but its scope is unknown. Ask formally whether other users have the same experience.
Of means whether. Asking about other users checks scope without assuming an organisation-wide outage.
S=Ik|V=heb|O=alleen de gegevens die voor deze melding nodig zijn|C=nodig.
I only need the details that are necessary for this report.
A customer offers a large amount of unrelated personal information. Explain formally that you only need details relevant to this support report.
Alleen limits what is needed. The relative clause die ... nodig zijn modifies plural gegevens.
Do not send your password with the report.
A customer is about to submit a support report and considers including their password. Politely instruct them not to include it.
Mee sturen is one separable verb: stuur ... mee. This is an instruction, not a description of something already sent.
After your explanation, I can classify the report more accurately.
A customer has added useful details to a request. Explain formally that their explanation allows you to categorise the report better.
The whole time phrase is first, followed by kan and ik. Better classification does not itself establish the technical cause.
Ik kan de melding na uw uitleg beter indelen.
After your explanation, I can classify the report more accurately.
Starting with ik changes the order, not the explanation's effect on classification.
When are you available for a short support call?
You need to arrange a brief support conversation with a customer. Ask formally when they are available.
Bent agrees with formal u even though the subject follows the verb. Beschikbaar concerns the customer's schedule.
Can I call you back tomorrow at ten?
You need more time to investigate a customer's request. Ask formally whether you may call them back tomorrow at ten.
The proposed time is specific; the question is not a promise that the problem will be solved by then.
The appointment is in the calendar for Tuesday morning.
A customer asks when the support appointment is scheduled. Confirm formally that it is in the calendar for Tuesday morning.
Voormiddag is standard Belgian wording for morning before noon. Staat describes the scheduled entry.
Could you stay at your device during the appointment?
You will need a customer's observations during a remote support appointment. Ask formally whether they can remain beside their device.
Tijdens limits the request to the appointment. Bij uw toestel describes physical availability, not remote access rights.
Unfortunately, I cannot make the proposed appointment.
A colleague proposes a support appointment that conflicts with your schedule. Politely explain that you cannot attend that proposed slot.
Een afspraak halen means manage to attend it here. This does not cancel the underlying support request.
Could we move the conversation to the afternoon?
A support conversation is planned at an unsuitable time. Ask politely whether the participants could move it to the afternoon.
Zouden we includes the speaker in the proposed change. Namiddag is standard Belgian wording for afternoon.
I have confirmed the appointment with the user.
A teammate asks whether the user knows the arranged support time. Report that you have confirmed the appointment with that user.
Confirmed scheduling is distinct from completed troubleshooting. Met identifies the person involved in confirmation.
S=Ik|V=plan|O=de afspraak|PART=in|G=zodra u uw beschikbaarheid doorgeeft.
I will schedule the appointment as soon as you provide your availability.
A customer wants an appointment but has not provided suitable times. Explain formally that you will schedule it after receiving their availability.
Inplannen splits in the main clause. Doorgeeft stays joined at the end of the subordinate clause introduced by zodra.
Before the conversation, I will send you a short confirmation.
You have agreed on a support call with a customer. Promise formally to send a short confirmation before the call.
U is the recipient and een korte bevestiging is the item sent. The time phrase is one first constituent.
Ik stuur u voor het gesprek een korte bevestiging.
Before the conversation, I will send you a short confirmation.
The subject comes first; the same confirmation and before-call timing remain unchanged.
T=Tijdens ons vorige gesprek|PAST=spraken|S=we|O=een nieuw tijdstip|PART=af.
During our previous conversation, we agreed on a new time.
A customer asks why the calendar entry differs from the first proposal. Remind them formally that a new time was agreed in the previous conversation.
Spraken af is plural past of afspreken. Nieuw means a newly agreed time, not an unfamiliar existing one.
May I look at your shared screen?
You are beginning remote support with a customer. Ask formally for permission to view the screen they are sharing.
Mag requests permission. The request is limited to the shared screen, not the customer's entire account.
IM=Sluit|O=persoonlijke vensters|A=alstublieft|G=voordat u het scherm deelt.
Please close personal windows before sharing the screen.
A customer is about to share a screen for troubleshooting. Politely ask them to close unrelated personal windows first.
Voordat requires closing the windows before sharing. Sluiten does not mean deleting their contents.
I will first take a look together with you.
A customer asks how the remote support will begin. Explain formally that you will start by looking together with them.
Kijk ... mee is separable. First looking together does not grant control of the customer's device.
Can you see the window I mean?
During a remote support call, you refer to a particular window. Ask the customer formally whether they can see the intended one.
Dat ik bedoel is a relative clause modifying het venster; its finite bedoel is final.
Could you carry out the next step yourself?
You can view a customer's screen but are not operating their device. Ask formally whether they can perform the next instructed step.
Zelf identifies the customer as the person doing the action. The support agent is not claiming to control the device.
I do not need your password for screen sharing.
A customer offers their password when starting screen sharing. Explain formally that you do not need it for sharing the screen.
Niet negates need for a particular item. This does not authorise asking for verification codes instead.
You can stop sharing at any time.
A customer wants control over a remote support session. Explain formally that they can stop screen sharing whenever they wish.
U is the person able to stop sharing. Op elk moment specifies that the option remains available throughout.
S=Ik|AUX=heb|O=de gedeelde informatie|T=alleen voor deze controle|PT=gebruikt.
I have used the shared information only for this check.
After a remote support check, a customer asks what you used their shared information for. State formally that its use was limited to that check.
Alleen restricts the stated use. This is a report about what was done, not a broad organisational privacy guarantee.
S=Ik|V=leg|PART=uit|G=wat u kunt doen voordat we beginnen.
I will explain what you can do before we start.
A customer is unsure what to prepare for remote support. Promise formally to explain their preparatory options before the session starts.
Leg ... uit is separable; what you can do is the explanation's content. Before starting describes the preparation stage.
I will end the connection after the check.
A customer asks when the remote support connection will close. Promise formally to end it after the check.
The promise concerns ending the connection, not deleting the customer's files or the ticket history.
I am investigating your report further.
A customer asks for an update while the issue is still under investigation. Tell them formally that you are continuing the investigation.
Verder indicates continuation; it does not claim that the cause has already been established.
I do not know the cause yet at this point.
A customer asks why their issue occurs, but you have no confirmed diagnosis. Explain formally that the cause is not yet known to you.
Nog niet preserves the possibility of later discovery. The sentence avoids presenting a guess as a confirmed cause.
I will update you on progress later today.
A customer needs to know when they will receive news. Commit formally to providing a progress update before today is over.
Vandaag nog promises same-day communication, not necessarily a same-day resolution. Informeren over introduces the topic.
I cannot confirm a recovery time yet.
A customer asks for a definite recovery time before one is known. Explain formally that you cannot confirm that time yet.
Nog niet negates current ability to confirm. It does not predict that recovery will be impossible.
The next check concerns your access rights.
A customer asks what you will investigate next. Explain formally that the next check will concern their access rights.
Gaan over is concern/be about. The sentence does not say their rights are already known to be incorrect.
Can you continue working with this temporary procedure for now?
A permanent fix is not ready, but you have proposed a temporary way to work. Ask formally whether that lets the customer continue for now.
Verderwerken is a bare infinitive after kunt. The temporary procedure is not presented as a permanent fix.
S=Ik|V=neem|A=opnieuw|O=contact met u|PART=op|G=zodra ik meer weet.
I will contact you again as soon as I know more.
A customer is waiting for new findings. Promise formally to contact them again when you have more information.
Contact opnemen met is a fixed expression. Zodra sets the trigger; no specific recovery time is promised.
S=Ik|AUX=heb|O=de verwachte volgende stap|L=in het ticket|PT=beschreven.
I have described the expected next step in the ticket.
A colleague asks whether the waiting customer can see what comes next. Explain that the expected next step is documented in the ticket.
Verwachte marks an expectation rather than a guaranteed outcome. Documentation is completed, while the step itself may still be pending.
Which task are you unable to carry out because of this problem?
A customer reports a problem without explaining its impact. Ask formally which work task it prevents them from completing.
The question identifies actual task impact. It does not assume that every task or every user is blocked.
S=Ik|V=kan|NEG=niet|I=beloven|G=dat de oplossing vandaag klaar is.
I cannot promise that the solution will be ready today.
A customer requests a guarantee you cannot responsibly give. Explain formally that you cannot promise a completed solution today.
Cannot promise is weaker than saying the solution definitely will not be ready. The dat-clause states the unconfirmed outcome.
Can you carry out the original task again now?
After support work, ask the customer formally whether they can now perform the task that originally failed.
Nu weer asks about restored practical ability. It does not ask whether the customer has approved every technical change.
Before ending a support conversation, ask the customer formally which parts of their experience are still unresolved.
Nog niet asks about remaining issues. It does not presume that every part of the request has been fixed.
May I close the ticket after your confirmation?
A customer's result appears satisfactory, but you want agreement before closure. Ask formally whether you may close the ticket after their confirmation.
Na uw bevestiging makes confirmation a prerequisite. Afsluiten is closing the record, not deleting it.
S=Het ticket|V=blijft|C=open|G=totdat u het resultaat hebt bevestigd.
The ticket will remain open until you have confirmed the result.
A customer has not yet tested the result of support work. Explain formally that the ticket stays open until they confirm it.
Totdat names the ending condition for the open state. Hebt bevestigd is a final perfect group.
I have documented the steps carried out in the report.
A colleague asks what record remains after a support action. Explain that the performed steps have been documented in the report.
Uitgevoerde is an attributive participle modifying plural stappen. Documentation is not a claim that all possible problems are resolved.
Please keep the ticket number for any follow-up.
You are finishing a support call with a customer. Politely ask them to retain the reference number in case follow-up is needed.
Eventuele means possible, not eventual in English. Retaining the reference does not require keeping a password or secret code.
G=Als het probleem terugkomt,|IM=verwijs|A=dan|PP=naar dit ticket.
If the problem returns, refer to this ticket.
You are explaining what a customer should do if the same problem recurs later. Give a formal instruction to refer to the current ticket.
The main clause is an imperative with understood addressed subject; dan is an adverb, not a subject. Recurrence is conditional, not predicted.
Closing does not mean deleting here.
A colleague confuses closing a support ticket with deleting it. Explain that the two actions are different in this workflow.
Afsluiten is an infinitive used as the subject. Verwijderen names the distinct action denied by niet.
V=Heeft|S=u|T=nog|O=hulp bij een van de stappen|C=nodig?
Do you still need help with any of the steps?
You have explained a support procedure to a customer. Ask formally whether they still need help with any step before you finish.
Hebben nodig expresses need. Een van de stappen selects any one step without assuming every step remains unclear.
S=Ik|MOD=zal|O=de samenvatting van dit gesprek|PP=aan uw ticket|I=toevoegen.
I will add the summary of this conversation to your ticket.
You are finishing a customer's support call. Promise formally to attach a summary of the conversation to their ticket.
Toevoegen aan names the destination. It is a documentation commitment, not a claim that the summary has already been attached.
